title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair loop changes verifier-detected safety violations of LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 deterministic intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal (requested model: gpt-5-mini) produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the same shared LLM proposal examined by a deterministic netops validator with up to one automated repair iteration invoked only if the validator flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002. The archived analysis used the exact McNemar two-sided convention implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); this yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed single discordant pair (implementation detail in Methods). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Total model-call accounting recorded 501 provider calls and a single repair-stage call. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the marginal numeric verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though one archived discordant episode shows the loop corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for NetOps tasks: translating operator intent into device configuration, planning multi-step changes, and producing candidate repair sequences. Empirical system reports and recent surveys emphasize that operational safety often depends more on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, rollback—than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common practical mitigation pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the model generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied when violations appear. Despite conceptual consensus, there is limited controlled, artifact-backed measurement isolating the verifier’s marginal contribution when holding the model’s initial proposal fixed. To address this, we preregistered and executed a paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under a canonical, verifier-scoped synthetic workload. Our objective was narrowly operational: given identical initial proposals (shared-initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tooling and formal analyses for network configurations (header-space analysis and route-model verifiers) can check reachability, isolation, and update-safety and are widely cited in NetOps verification literature [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems propose or instantiate LLM-based intent translators and stress the need for validators and guardrails to attain operational reliability [INTA, 2025; Confucius, 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are proposed across structured-generation domains as a practical method to reduce incorrect outputs and to produce machine-checkable artifacts [PoeTone; INTA]. Failure-mode analyses of LLM-driven automation document hallucination, overconfidence, and tool-integration errors and motivate verifier-in-the-loop pipelines [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. Nevertheless, the supplied literature and system reports rarely report controlled ablations that quantify a verifier’s effect size under reproducible, artifact-backed conditions; our study contributes one such preregistered, archived measurement and positions its scope relative to those prior systems.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan: The full preregistration (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026) froze the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generation seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before execution. Key confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). The preregistered primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations.

Task generation and strata: We generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks using the archived deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and stratified allocation: VLAN-change (167 tasks), ACL-change (167), static-route-change (166). The task payloads and generator seeds are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. To ensure construct validity with respect to the chosen verifier, the task generator constrained allowed_fields to {admin, mtu, vlan}; tasks that referenced unmodeled features would have been routed to an 'unmodeled-feature' cohort and excluded per preregistration (no confirmatory exclusions occurred in this run). Each task includes an initial_state, expected_final_state, and an explicit required_sequence (examples archived under representative_tasks in the evidence bundle).

Generation semantics and experimental control: We used preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false. For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal (the shared candidate) which was recorded and served as the baseline output; the guarded condition evaluated that identical shared candidate with the deterministic validator and invoked the repair-stage call only if the validator reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. This semantic isolates the marginal effect of verification and a single repair iteration conditional on identical proposals, avoiding conflation with verifier-guided regeneration strategies. The design choice was preregistered to answer the narrowly framed operational question: what is the verifier+repair effect when the model’s initial proposal is fixed?

Models, adapter, and validator: Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); archived model_configuration.json records model configuration (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation semantics). The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator-spec and severity mapping archived). The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Primary statistical test and exact implementation: The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements this by treating the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 and performing an exact binomial test B(n, 0.5) on the observed count n10 (or equivalently on n01). For two-sided reporting the executor computes p_two-sided = 2 * min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} under X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), with the conventional truncation at 1.0. With the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0, hence n = 1) the two one-sided tail probabilities are both 0.5, so p_two-sided = 2×0.5 = 1.0; this precise computational rule and rationale are recorded in the archived analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report the archived exact two-sided p = 1.00 and place it in context (Results).

Bootstrap CI and resampling semantics: We computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute difference using B = 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729, resampling unit = task/pair while preserving pairing (each resample draws 500 pairs with replacement). The archived analysis artifacts include bootstrap parameters and resampling code references.

Missingness, retries, and stopping rule: Preregistered retry policy allowed up to 2 automated retries for transient model-provider errors; the run stopped when the preregistered confirmatory pairs (N = 500) completed or when the adapter model-call budget was reached. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501, completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 pairs × 2 conditions recorded under shared-initial semantics with one repair-stage call), and failed_episode_count = 0. All provider calls, responses, and retry metadata are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes: The experiment completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500 and repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar two-sided result and interpretation: As implemented in the archived analysis executor, the exact McNemar two-sided p-value computed from the discordant-pair binomial (n = 1) is p = 1.00. This occurs because, for n = 1, the two-sided exact rule yields p = 2 × min{0.5, 0.5} = 1.00. The archived analysis also provides a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference: [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). These numeric results are present in analysis/results.json and in the associated CSV artifacts.

Repair activity and discordant-pair provenance: Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1 across the entire run. That single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1), i.e., the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The execution and scoring artifacts archive per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses (when invoked), and provider-call traces. The raw results file execution/raw_results.jsonl contains the complete per-task records and is the deterministic source for locating the discordant episode: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. Because exactly one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, that filter deterministically returns the single episode and its repair-stage provider-call trace. Representative per-task exemplar files and provider-call traces are included in the evidence bundle (see artifact_examples and representative_tasks entries).

Secondary and subgroup analyses: The preregistered per-violation-class secondary analyses were uninformative because observed violation counts were nearly zero—there were no meaningful counts to support class-level inference. The low baseline error prevalence (499/500 passes) created a ceiling effect that reduces power to detect small absolute gains on the pass-rate metric. The preregistration anticipated an approximate baseline p_b ≈ 0.30 for power planning; observed prevalence was far lower, invalidating that assumption and explaining the small observed absolute effect. Analysis artifacts include a missingness_summary.csv and a contamination_summary.csv; both indicate no exclusions, no missing pairs, and no contamination events in this run. All numeric tables and logs are archived under analysis/ and execution/ paths recorded in the manifest.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation and limits: The experiment quantifies the marginal verifier+repair effect under a constrained, well-specified operational regime: a single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), deterministic shared-initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic validator modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and a single automated repair iteration. In that regime the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals, so the measured absolute effect on the pass-rate metric is small (0.002). Crucially, this outcome should not be read as evidence that verifiers are unnecessary: (1) the verifier produced at least one concrete correction (the single discordant episode), demonstrating corrective potential; (2) in workloads with higher baseline error prevalence, broader property coverage by the verifier, or heterogeneous vendor CLIs, verifier+repair gains could be much larger.

Design choice implications: The shared_initial_candidate generation semantics intentionally isolates verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals; it answers the specific operational question: how much additional safety does a verifier+single-repair provide when the model’s proposed change is fixed? It does not measure the effect of verifier-guided regeneration, iterative multi-repair loops, or independent-condition generation (each of which answers different operational tradeoffs and may yield different effect sizes). Practitioners should align experimental semantics with operational deployment semantics when estimating guardrail benefits.

Threats to internal and construct validity: Internal validity is supported by the preregistered paired design, deterministic generation seeds, and automated exclusion rules (no manual adjudication). Nonetheless, the ceiling effect (very low baseline error prevalence) undermines the statistical sensitivity for detecting small improvements on the pass-rate metric. Construct validity depends on whether the chosen verifier’s property set aligns with operational safety concerns: our verification pass/fail is a composite defined relative to the verifier’s modeled properties and severity mapping (archived in validator-spec artifacts). If a production operator cares about additional properties not modeled by the verifier (e.g., dynamic protocol state, vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies), the measured pass-rate difference here will understate the real-world need for extended guardrails.

External validity and generalization: The study used a single requested model family, one deterministic validator, and a synthetic task corpus limited to a small configuration feature set; results therefore do not establish general multi-model or cross-vendor generality. Similarly, production workloads with noisy, underspecified, or multi-feature intents may produce higher baseline failure rates and larger verifier benefit. We emphasize that our result is a conditional measurement: under the tested conditions the verifier+single-repair produced a small absolute improvement because the model’s proposals were already nearly correct.

Operational recommendations grounded in the archive: (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before investing heavily in automated repair budgets—when baseline error is already very low, marginal pass-rate gains from expensive verifier+repair pipelines may be small for the pass-rate metric. (2) Prefer verifier designs whose modeled property set aligns with the operator’s safety-critical constraints; the archived validator-spec and mapping files should be inspected to determine coverage. (3) Choose generation semantics (shared-initial vs verifier-guided regeneration) that match the target operational question: if the goal is to minimize machine-inserted changes at any cost, shared-initial semantics are appropriate; if the goal is to maximize final-pass probability irrespective of regeneration costs, verifier-guided regeneration or larger repair budgets may be preferable. The evidence bundle contains the execution logs and exemplar repair traces to support these operational evaluations.

Reproducibility and artifact accessibility: All preregistration, task generator seeds and code, model-configuration, provider-call traces, raw LLM responses, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, execution logs, analysis CSVs, and the deterministic reconciliation manifest are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/* and analysis/* artifacts). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501, completed_episode_count = 1000, and observed repair_stage = 1. The exact initial master prompt used to initiate the autonomous research run is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is referenced in the Disclosure Statement below. The single discordant episode is locatable deterministically by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for baseline pass==0 and guarded pass==1; that file contains the validator violation codes and the repair-stage prompt/response for qualitative failure-mode analysis.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On the supplied synthetic verifier-scoped corpus and with the requested model/validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the two-sided binomial convention implemented). The result documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal error prevalence is extremely low and verifier coverage is constrained, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a verifier on this metric may be negligible, but the verifier can still correct rare but concrete failures (one archived corrected episode). We recommend that operators measure baseline error prevalence and verifier coverage on representative workloads and align generation/repair semantics with operational priorities; the archived evidence bundle supports deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; the task payloads in the archive show allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not necessarily generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 must be interpreted in that context and reflects the archived two-sided exact-binomial convention for n = 1 discordant pair.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair_id entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
